Sample one realization of the branching structure via UQ

Source: R/sampling_branching.r
sample_branching.Rd

Draws a single stochastic realization of the Hawkes branching structure by, for each event i, sampling whether it is a background event or was triggered by a specific earlier event j, using the fitted background probabilities and pairwise excitation weights. This is the "stochastic declustering" step: unlike thresholding bgprobs at a fixed cutoff (e.g. 0.5), it produces a proper Monte Carlo draw from the branching structure's posterior distribution given the fitted model, so repeated calls can be used to quantify uncertainty in any downstream summary that depends on which events are "background" vs. "triggered" (see sample_branching_multi()).

Usage

sample_branching(bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights)

Arguments

bgprobs

Numeric vector of fitted background probabilities, one per event, in the same row order as events$events (e.g. fit$bgprobs from fit_semihawkes()/em_step()).

pairs

A pair index from trigger_pairs(), with integer columns i (child/triggered event) and j (candidate parent event). Must be the same pairs object used to fit the fit whose bgprobs and pair_weights are supplied – the window parameters (window_days/window_dist) determine which parents are even candidates.

pair_weights

Numeric vector of excitation weights from trigger_pair_weights(), same length and row order as pairs. For each child i, bgprobs[i] + sum(pair_weights[pairs$i == i]) should equal 1 (up to floating-point error); see check_branching_weights().

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_branching_sample" with a single element mark: an integer vector, one entry per event, 0 if that event was sampled as background, or the row index (into events$events) of its sampled parent otherwise.

Details

For each event i:

  • Draw u ~ Uniform(0, 1).

  • If u < bgprobs[i], mark i as background (mark[i] = 0).

  • Otherwise, find all candidate parents j of i (rows of pairs with pairs$i == i), and assign i to the parent j whose cumulative excitation-weight interval contains u, i.e. sample j with probability proportional to pair_weights among i's candidate parents.

See also

sample_branching_multi() for repeated draws, check_branching_weights() to validate bgprobs/pair_weights consistency before sampling.

Examples

# A tiny synthetic case: 4 events, with `bgprobs` and `pair_weights`
# chosen so each event's total probability sums to 1 (see
# `check_branching_weights()`). Event 1 has no candidate parents, so it
# is always background.
bgprobs <- c(1, 0.4, 0.5, 0.2)
pairs <- data.frame(i = as.integer(c(2, 3, 3, 4, 4)),
                    j = as.integer(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3)))
pair_weights <- c(0.6, 0.3, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3)

set.seed(1)
draw <- sample_branching(bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights)
draw
#> <semihawkes_branching_sample>
#>   4 events, 2 background (50.0%), 2 triggered
draw$mark # 0 = background; otherwise the sampled parent's row index
#> [1] 0 0 1 3

# See `vignette("branching-structure-uq")` for the full workflow on a
# fitted `semihawkes_fit` object.
